title: Hiring plans, jobseeker support and Work Pass calibration amid Middle East cost pressures
asked: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked what the Government assesses the impact of energy and business costs to be on hiring prospects for jobseekers, including graduates and mid-career entrants, whether there are signs of slower entry-level job creation or longer job searches, and what further measures are being considered to support employment. Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked whether business hiring is more subdued, which sectors are most affected, and what further measures are being taken to support employment growth.
asked_by: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Liang Eng Hwa
response: Dr Tan See Leng said energy-intensive industries and outward-oriented sectors saw the most impact from higher energy costs, and that firms have become more cautious: the share intending to hire in the next three months fell from 54.6% in February 2026 to 44.6% in March 2026, with early signs of stabilisation in April. Jobseekers who need help can use Workforce Singapore and SkillsFuture Singapore career matching services, and MOM stands ready to provide further support if necessary. He said there has been no shift in firms' hiring preferences between local and foreign workers, resident employment grew in the first quarter of 2026, and Work Pass policies are continually calibrated, including higher Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries from January 2027.

key_points.point: Energy-intensive industries and outward-oriented sectors saw the most impact from increased energy costs.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: Energy-intensive industries and outward-oriented sectors saw the most impact from increased energy costs.

key_points.point: The proportion of firms intending to hire in the next three months fell from 54.6% in February 2026 to 44.6% in March 2026.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: fell from 54.6% in February 2026 to 44.6% in March 2026

key_points.point: There were early signs of stabilisation in April, supported by Economic Development Board and Department of Statistics data.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: there were early signs of stabilisation in April

key_points.point: Jobseekers needing help can tap Workforce Singapore and SkillsFuture Singapore career matching services and programmes.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: All jobseekers who need assistance can tap on Workforce Singapore and SkillsFuture Singapore's suite of career matching services and programmes.

key_points.point: MOM stands ready to provide further support to jobseekers depending on economic and job market conditions.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: MOM stands ready to provide further support to jobseekers, if necessary

key_points.point: No shift has been observed in firms' hiring preferences between local workers and foreign workers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: We have not seen any shifts at the moment in firms' hiring preferences.

key_points.point: Resident employment continued to grow in the first quarter of 2026, higher than the first quarter of 2025.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: Our resident employment continued to grow in the first quarter of 2026

key_points.point: Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries will increase from January 2027.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: we announced an increase in Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries that will take effect from January 2027

key_points.point: The COMPASS Shortage Occupation List is regularly reviewed to remove occupations no longer in shortage.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: We also regularly review the Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS) Shortage Occupation List (SOL) to remove occupations that are no longer in shortage.

key_points.point: He said it is premature to conclude on long-term structural impact on industry transformation while the crisis is still unfolding.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: it is premature today to conclude on the long-term structural impact related to the industry transformation

key_points.point: The crisis is likely to accelerate existing structural shifts such as supply chain diversification and digitalisation.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: the crisis is likely to accelerate the existing structural shifts that are already underway in the entire global economy

key_points.point: Singapore has committed not to impose export restrictions on downstream refined products.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: we will not impose any export restriction

key_points.point: An Economic Strategy Review report is being prepared and will be released in due time.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: I had the opportunity of reading the draft of the Economic Strategy Review report.

left_open: Whether there are signs of slower entry-level job creation or longer job searches
What further measures are being considered beyond the existing Workforce Singapore and SkillsFuture Singapore services
Whether Work Pass policies would be further calibrated if mid-career PMETs face weaker hiring
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered hiring preferences between local and foreign workers, Work Pass calibration, long-term structural change in energy industries, and workforce planning under persistent uncertainty.
